shared_design.card_schema: Same field layout as the sibling batch (SCN-riverbank, SCN-field-hedge-burrow): scene_id, inherits, layer, int_ext, form, stories, source_chapter, culture_ref, period, structure[], materials[], details[], interior (INT only: layout, openings for 05-scenes/lighting, furniture_tone), scale_notes, negative[], prompt_ready_en. Added for dream scenes: grows_from (copied from scenes/index.json plus design_growth) and dream_design_language. Every structure/materials/details item carries src (a structured_story paragraph id) or inferred:true + culture_ref + why.
shared_design.culture_basis: culture.json has no architecture entries (it covers etiquette, dress, games, food, lessons and verse). Architectural style is therefore designed from world.json frame (Oxford, 1862, clergyman-scholar household), world.json wonderland_real_counterparts (cp-*), geography.json settlement.architecture_style, and the family villa fixed in SCN-riverbank architecture (gabled polychrome-brick Gothic Revival). CUL-* entries are cited where a custom drives a built element (CUL-016 card court -> suit-shaped beds, tiles and panels; CUL-019 tea; CUL-023 pepper; CUL-013/017 croquet; CUL-006 court procedure).
shared_design.dream_language_rule: Ruling 5.2 A: each dream space is built from real 1860s Oxford and English materials and forms (honey oolitic limestone, polychrome brick, Welsh slate, long-straw thatch, Gothic Revival oak, encaustic tile, cast iron), then altered in one legible way that grows out of its waking detail: the service wing detached (Duchess), a thatched farmhouse with ear chimneys and fur-like thatch (March Hare), a college garden door grown into a tree, carpet bedding cut in card suits, a croquet lawn laid over ridge-and-furrow, a seaside emptied of people, a book-illustration court in the card colours.
shared_design.garden: SCN-queens-garden is a container with no card, so SCN-rose-tree-yard sets the garden's shared materials (honey limestone, buff gravel, clipped box and yew) and SCN-croquet-ground and SCN-gryphon-sunning-spot repeat them by value with inherits:null (inherits must point to a scene card on the parent chain).
shared_design.scale_reference: Alice = 135 cm at 1:1, as set by the sibling SCN-riverbank card. Size beats in this batch: pigeon treetop (1:10 miniature canopy + 1:1 nest set), Duchess's house (1:6 four-foot miniature on arrival; full-size hero house with Alice at about knee height to the footmen at 'nine inches'), March Hare's house (full-size facade, Alice about 60 cm apparent at 'two feet'), garden arrival (3x oversized bed edge at 'a foot high'), courtroom growth (2/3-scale jury-box corner and dais + breakaway jury-box). All other scenes are 1:1.

key_decisions: Duchess's house: the text gives 'four feet high' and 'nine inches' but the footmen are human performers (SUP-002). So the four-foot house is a 1:6 miniature used only for the arrival shot. The doorstep plays on a full-size house, with Alice at about knee height to the footmen, rather than at a literal 1:6 ratio. The kitchen and the baby-to-pig exit are shot at 1:1.
Duchess's kitchen: the family's closed range is dreamed back into an open hearth with a crane-hung cauldron, following the source's 'leaning over the fire, stirring a large cauldron'.
The courtroom's jury-box is raised 1.2 m because ch012-p01 says the jurors fall 'on to the heads of the crowd below'.
The croquet-ground's ridges and furrows are designed as real medieval ridge-and-furrow grassland, a feature common in Oxfordshire, covered in close-mown turf.
The tea-party gets a tall-case clock stopped at six. It is a fixed set piece and does not replace the Hatter's watch prop (SUP-012).
Weathered stone griffin on a garden gate-pier = the waking seed of the Gryphon; plainly a statue, negatives forbid animation

interior.openings are given for SCN-duchess-kitchen and SCN-courtroom, including wall, size and sill height. For exteriors, the sun and shade sources come from the structure items: the horse-chestnut, the cedar, the ha-ha and the open shore.

Some items in these cards are props that 06-art/prop owns: the great letter, the paint pots, the tea-things, the slates and the tarts. They are marked (props owned by 06-art/prop). The architecture cards only fix where these items sit.
The scale_notes in each card set how each size beat in SUP-003 is built. If the storyboard needs a different ratio for a beat, that change should come back through 05-scenes/architecture.
